espn-604011.headline: One more go at Fiji, and last place for the loser
beats: The 11th-place final at Allianz Stadium, London, is a straight rematch of Udine on 21 November, where Fiji won 21–16 with two tries in seven minutes after half-time. Italy finished the pool without a win, and have lost seven straight.
Italy lose flyhalf Domingo Miotti, who left Udine in the 48th minute with a hamstring injury, and prop Simone Ferrari, who withdrew an hour before kickoff there. Lynagh is back.

Fiji won that game while kicking possession away, Frank Lomani box-kicking even from inside Italy's 22, and Italy read them well enough to make it close. Win this time and Italy go above Fiji in the world rankings, into 10th.
Italy go to Scotland in February. Fiji's next Test is Spain at the World Cup, which leaves this as the last word for some time.

espn-604012.headline: Beat the world champions, win a half-empty Twickenham
beats: Ireland beat South Africa 20–17 on 21 November and finished third in the North, one point behind England. That earns them the fifth-place final, and ticket sales point to a crowd under half of the stadium's 82,000.
Andy Farrell has dismissed the idea that this is an anti-climax. He may have to make the point without Dan Sheehan, whose yellow card against South Africa has been upgraded to a red.

Australia's coach, Les Kiss, used to run Ireland's defence. His side lost to Ireland 33–31 in Sydney in July, to a late Thomas Clarkson try converted by Sam Prendergast. In October they conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand.
A win lifts Ireland to third in the world rankings, above France, who will be busy playing the actual final.

espn-604013.headline: Wales rotate against the side they barely beat
beats: Steve Tandy has promised changes for the 9th-place final at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium, after eleven of his players started all three November Tests. Three weeks ago in Cardiff, Wales needed a Josh Adams try in the 69th minute to see Japan off 28–21.

Japan have not looked like that side since. They conceded 78 to England and then 67 to Scotland, with one try at Murrayfield in reply. Wales beat New Zealand in between, then lost to Australia by three.
Win by 16 or more and Japan send Wales down to 11th, below Fiji and Japan. That would take the kind of margin Japan have lately been conceding, not scoring.
Wales go to France in February, in a Six Nations with no room for experiments. This is the last cheap look Tandy gets, provided it stays cheap.

espn-604014.headline: New Zealand get seven days to undo 37–12
beats: England have never beaten New Zealand in three consecutive Tests. They won 33–19 last November and 37–12 on 21 November on this ground, the most points New Zealand have ever conceded to a Northern Hemisphere nation.
That defeat followed a 35–28 loss to Wales. Dave Rennie said his side were "miles off" and that he is a "big part of that". New Zealand Rugby say he stays whatever happens in this third-place final.
Tommy Freeman missed last week's win with a quad issue and is back in the squad. Win by 16 or more and England go third in the world, with New Zealand down to fifth. The margin last time was 25.
New Zealand's next Test is Chile at home in the World Cup, next October. That is a long time to sit on whatever happens here.

espn-604015.headline: Scotland's home game for seventh is in London
beats: Scotland are the home side at Allianz Stadium, playing for seventh place in the curtain-raiser to the final between South Africa and France. France got there by beating Argentina 45-17 a week earlier.

The sides scored 85 points between them in Cordoba in July, and Scotland took it 47-38. Argentina have since conceded 42 to Ireland and 45 to France. Scotland put 67 on Japan, with a hat-trick from Liam McConnell, and the case for letting him loose on Argentina is already being made.
Argentina have won two Tests this year. If they win this one by 16 or more, they take sixth in the world rankings from Scotland.
Scotland have Italy at home in February. Argentina's next game is Canada at the World Cup in October 2027, which is a long time to live with whichever number they finish on.

espn-604016.headline: Banned over France, Erasmus will stream the rematch
beats: Rassie Erasmus's six-game ban followed South Africa's 21–19 loss in Paris on 13 November, after he questioned whether "match-fixing" and "manipulation" was occurring in rugby. He hosted a watch-along from the team hotel for the 20–17 defeat to Ireland, and has announced another for the final.

His staff deny taking instructions from him. They have made seven changes anyway: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu moves to fullback for the injured Damian Willemse, Manie Libbok takes the flyhalf jersey, and Emmanuel Tshituka could debut off the bench.
France arrive on five straight wins, the latest 45–17 over Argentina with seven tries. Win by 16 or more and they go top of the world rankings, above South Africa.
South Africa have lost their last two by five points combined. Their coach will watch this one on a screen, like everyone else.
